claims.text: Minor Cr doping of a magnetic high-entropy alloy will increase its coercive field.
Replacing part of the Co with Cr will promote controlled nanoscale phase decomposition or precipitate formation in the proposed NiFeCoCr-based alloy.
Arc-melting followed by rapid cooling will lock in the proposed nanostructured decomposed state.
In prior AlCoFeNi work, replacing Co with Cr promoted a mixture of ordered B2 and disordered BCC regions.
The nanoscale heterogeneities produced by Cr doping will act as domain-wall pinning centers.
Enhanced domain-wall pinning will hinder magnetization reversal and thereby increase coercivity.
The Cr-modified alloy will have a higher coercive field than an otherwise identically processed alloy without the Cr substitution.
The coercivity-enhancing effect should hold for arc-melted, rapidly cooled samples measured at ambient temperature.
Excessive Cr or substantial changes in cooling rate may produce unwanted secondary phases or degrade other magnetic properties.
Cr substitution may compromise saturation magnetization.
The starting NiFeCoCr-based alloy has a uniform microstructure.

contradictions.description: The conditions describe processing at room temperature while the intervention requires arc-melting, which necessarily involves a molten, high-temperature state. The wording may have intended ambient-temperature magnetic measurement, but it does not clearly make that distinction.
